nodes.description: If respiratory inner arms fail, mucus clearance from the airways falls, as in other PCD forms, leading to chronic sinus and bronchial infection and bronchiectasis. Clearance has not been measured in a CILD50 patient, and the airway phenotypes below rest on very few patients, so this step is inferred from the general PCD mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic mutations in DNAH7 cause asthenozoospermia by impairing the integrality of axoneme structure.
evidence.snippet: Dynein protein arms play a crucial role in the motility of both the cilia and flagella, and defects in these proteins generally impair the axoneme structure and cause primary ciliary dyskinesia.

nodes.description: In one PCD patient whose respiratory cilia lacked inner dynein arms and moved abnormally, DNAH7 was made in the cell but missing from the cilia. That patient was not genotyped, so the lesion may have been in another gene. The only patient with biallelic DNAH7 variants whose airway cilia were examined, a man homozygous for a frameshift, had normal ciliary ultrastructure on electron microscopy. An inner-arm defect in airway cilia is therefore expected from DNAH7's location but has not been shown in a genotyped CILD50 patient.
